title: PlaybackInfo reads a source once
description: One PlaybackInfo reads the same media_sources row three or four times and writes on every call.
acceptanceCriteria: Counted by a pgx tracer over the statements one PlaybackInfo request sends (GET or POST), at most one statement names media_sources for each source in the reply, the keyframe index included, in every branch: direct play, copy, re-encode, a live job joined, a refusal, and the fall-back to the default tracks

That bound holds for the source that costs four reads today (font attachments, a text subtitle track while no worker is alive, a copyable video with a keyframe index, a DeviceProfile, on a replica with a transcodeStore), and for the same source with a worker alive (three today)
An item whose reply lists two sources sends at most two such statements, and at most one when MediaSourceId names one of them

No PlaybackInfo answers from an earlier call's read: after the row changes (a replaced file's new ETag, streams and keyframes), the next call on the same replica answers from the new row, its TranscodingUrl carrying the new tag

With no transcode job queued and the source's fonts stored (or none), no statement a PlaybackInfo request sends contains DELETE or UPDATE, whether as the statement, in a CTE or in an ON CONFLICT clause, in every branch of the first criterion, on an api replica with a transcodeStore and on one without; the replica's own heartbeats are not the request's statements
With no transcode job queued and a source whose fonts are not stored yet, the only statement with DELETE or UPDATE is the one enqueue of its fonts job, at most one per source per call
A transcode job queued longer than queueTimeout is still cancelled with 'no worker took the job' by the PlaybackInfo that needs a transcode and sees it, and is never offered as live

An offered transcode still has its reasons written exactly once per offered source (GET /Sessions lists them for the playing session), and transcode_reasons rows older than a day are still removed with only api replicas running, though by no statement of a PlaybackInfo while nothing is queued; a row younger than a day stays

jellyscale_playbackinfo_decisions_total (the task's jellyscale_playback_decisions_total) rises by exactly one per source the reply lists, under that source's method and under no other, in a table of: no profile without a transcodeStore; no profile with one; a profile that plays directly; re-encode; copy; a live job joined; a replica without a transcodeStore and no worker anywhere; the fall-back to the default tracks when the transcode cannot start
A source the reply lists as direct play because the item has no runtime, or because its media_sources row is gone, is counted as direct_play exactly once (today it is counted nowhere)
A refused PlaybackInfo raises jellyscale_playbackinfo_refusals_total by exactly one and no decision label, and a reply that lists two sources raises the decisions by exactly two, one for each
